scenario: AITA for keeping my son during my visitation instead of giving in to his mother? | I guess some backstory is due here. My ex and I have an 8 year old son, and we have been split up for a few years now. I have every other weekend parenting time along with a day during the week. It’s not enough time for me, but it’s what was legally decided through court. Her and I do not have the best relationship currently because I feel like I’m always being taken advantage of and I allow it because she always uses the “it’s for your son” excuse. I cherish my time with my son, but for the longest time, I allowed my ex to alter the parenting schedule to suit my son’s needs, whether for activities or family or if he just wasn’t feeling well. I always tried to be as accommodating as possible, even if it meant I didn’t see him for a week or more. Anyway, last Wednesday I was supposed to get him overnight, his mother called me and I asked if he could stay there since his cousin from out of town was staying with them. I reluctantly agreed but told her I wanted to get him Thursday instead. She agreed, and when Thursday came around, I texted her after work and said I was on my way to get him. She said they weren’t home, and I had to press her for information why. She decided to take the kids to a lake and said I needed to stop being grumpy because my son was having fun. We argued back and forth and since I did not drive all the way out to the lake to get him when I shouldn’t have had to in the first place, I told her that we should switch weekends (last weekend was hers, this one is mine) so that I had my make up time and his activities with her that fell on my weekend wouldn’t be interrupted. She refused, so now that my weekend is coming up, I’m not getting him at my regular time today because he’s at an amusement park with her family, and I am expected to give up even more of my valuable time tomorrow for their annual 4th of July party. Am I the asshole for putting my foot down and keeping my son during their family function so that I can enjoy time my son during my scheduled time?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is being an asshole (AITA) for keeping their son during their scheduled visitation time instead of letting the mother take him to a family event. Let me break this down step by step. First, the background: The person is a father who's been separated from his ex-wife for a few years. They have an 8-year-old son. The custody arrangement is every other weekend and one day during the week. The father feels this isn't enough time, but it's what the court decided. He's had a rocky relationship with his ex, feeling like she takes advantage of him, often using the "it's for the son" excuse. He's tried to be accommodating, sometimes not seeing his son for a week or more because of her requests. Last Wednesday, he was supposed to have his son overnight. The mother called and asked if the son could stay because her cousin was visiting. He agreed reluctantly but wanted to pick him up on Thursday. When Thursday came, he texted her after work to say he was on his way. She replied that they weren't home and were at a lake. They argued, and she told him to stop being grumpy because the son was having fun. He suggested swapping weekends so he could make up the time, but she refused. Now, his weekend is coming up, but the son is at an amusement park with her family today, and tomorrow there's a 4th of July party. He's expected to give up more time, and he's considering keeping his son during their scheduled time instead. So, is he the asshole for putting his foot down? Let me think about the key points: 1. Custody arrangement: Legally, he has every other weekend and a weekday. This is a court order, so it's supposed to be followed unless there's a change agreed upon by both parties or through the court. 2. Accommodation: He's been flexible, allowing her to change the schedule for various reasons, sometimes not seeing his son for a week or more. This shows he's been cooperative. 3. Recent incident: She asked to keep the son last Wednesday, he agreed but wanted him on Thursday. She then went to the lake without informing him properly, leading to an argument. He suggested swapping weekends, which she refused. 4. Current situation: His weekend is approaching, but the son is with her family for an amusement park and a 4th of July party. She expects him to give up more time. 5. His action: He's considering keeping his son during their scheduled time instead of letting her take him to the family function. Now, considering whether he's being an asshole: - He's following the court order, which is his legal right. She's expecting him to give up more time, but he's already been accommodating. - She didn't inform him properly about the lake trip, which could be seen as disrespectful or uncooperative. - He suggested swapping weekends, which is a reasonable compromise, but she refused. - By keeping his son during his scheduled time, he's asserting his rights as a parent, which is fair. - However, he might be seen as inflexible if he doesn't consider the family event, but given her past behavior, it's understandable he's upset. On the other hand, she's trying to spend time with her family, which is important, but she should have communicated better and respected his schedule. So, is he the asshole? I don't think so. He's within his rights to enforce the custody agreement, especially after being accommodating in the past. She needs to respect the court order and communicate better instead of expecting him to always give in.
